_note: Power is in kWh per sol (averaged over day and night). powerIn = uses, powerOut = makes. priority decides who keeps power in a shortage (higher stays on). produces/consumes are kg per sol. Power and output numbers are game balance unless a scienceNote says otherwise. size = footprint in tiles [width, height]. cropDiesAfter = sols in a row without power or water before a greenhouse crop dies (one bad sol just pauses growth). Greenhouse priority is above the water systems: crops die without power, a water tank just drains a bit.

buildings.name: Habitat
buildings.description: Home for your crew. Keeps them warm, pressurised and alive.
buildings.scienceNote: Mars nights can drop below -80 °C, so heating alone uses a lot of power.

buildings.name: Solar Array
buildings.description: Makes power from sunlight. How much depends on your landing sector.
buildings.scienceNote: Mars gets about 43% of the sunlight Earth does, and dust on the panels cuts that further.

buildings.name: Battery Bank
buildings.description: Stores spare power so the base keeps running when production drops.
buildings.scienceNote: Mars rovers use batteries to survive the freezing nights when their solar panels make nothing.

buildings.name: Fission Reactor
buildings.description: Steady power day and night, in any weather. Very expensive.
buildings.scienceNote: NASA tested a small fission reactor design called Kilopower in 2018. A 10-kilowatt unit like this makes about 246 kWh every sol, sun or no sun.

buildings.name: Oxygen Plant
buildings.description: Pulls carbon dioxide from the Martian air and turns it into breathable oxygen.
buildings.scienceNote: NASA's MOXIE experiment on the Perseverance rover proved this works on Mars, making 122 grams of oxygen between 2021 and 2023.

buildings.name: Ice Drill
buildings.description: Digs up icy soil and heats it to release water. Works best where there's lots of ice.
buildings.scienceNote: Most water on Mars is frozen in the ground or in the polar ice caps.

buildings.name: Water Recycler
buildings.description: Cleans used water so the crew can drink it again.
buildings.scienceNote: The International Space Station recycles about 98% of its water, including sweat and urine.

buildings.name: Greenhouse
buildings.description: Grows food under lights. Plants also make a little oxygen while they grow.
buildings.scienceNote: Plants need light, warmth and water. On Mars, sunlight is weak and nights are freezing, so greenhouses use a lot of power.

buildings.name: Rover Bay
buildings.description: Adds one more rover, so you can scavenge two places at once.
buildings.scienceNote: Radio signals take roughly 3 to 22 minutes to travel between Earth and Mars, so Mars rovers have to handle a lot of driving on their own.

buildings.name: Storm Shelter
buildings.description: A small room buried under regolith. The crew hides here when a solar storm hits.
buildings.scienceNote: Thick soil, rock and water block solar storm particles well. On the space station, crews shelter in the best-shielded modules.
